title: Imperatives in discourse
subtitle: Read commands within their appeal, reason, and promise.
overview: A command gains its force from the surrounding address, grounds, contrast, and promised outcome. Read the imperative as one move within an argument or scene.
Present and aorist imperative forms offer different aspectual viewpoints, but neither automatically means “keep doing” or “do once.”

items.grc: μετανοεῖτε καὶ πιστεύετε ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ.
items.en: Repent and believe in the gospel.

items.grc: μὴ ταρασσέσθω ὑμῶν ἡ καρδία· πιστεύετε εἰς τὸν θεόν.
items.en: Let not your heart be troubled; believe in God.
